MINUTES
  Special Meeting
  ALHAMBRA CITY COUNCIL
  February 24, 2025
  5:00 p.m.

ROLL CALL: At 5:14 p.m., on Monday, February 24, 2025, the Alhambra City Council met in the
Council Chambers of Alhambra City Hall.

PRESENT:  LEE, ANDRADE-STADLER, MAZA, WANG
ABSENT:  MALONEY

Officials Present: City Manager Binnquist, Assistant City Manager Garcia, Deputy City Manager
Hembree, City Attorney Montes, City Clerk Myles, Director of Parks and Recreation Macias, Director
of Finance Lieu, Director of Community Development Ho, Director of Public Works and Utilities Ahlen,
Chief of Police Kennedy, Chief of Fire Department Ragusa, Director of Library Services LohGuan,
Director of Human Resources Ko, Manager Analyst Alvarez

FLAG SALUTE:  Mayor Wang

LAND ACKNOWLEDGEMENT: We acknowledge that the land on which we are gathered is the
traditional, ancestral, and unceded territory of the Gabrielino/Tongva peoples. We seek to prioritize
respect for the historic culture and contemporary presence of the native peoples throughout California,
especially in the greater Los Angeles/Alhambra area. We come with respect and gratitude for the
Gabrielino/Tongva people who still consider themselves the caretakers of this land. It is through their
examples that we are reminded of our greater responsibility to take care of Mother Earth and to take
care of each other.

CITY CLERK REPORT - NOTICE NO. N2M25-17

The City Clerk hereby reported that she duly gave notice of the special meeting of the City Council
being held this evening pursuant to the order of the Mayor and in accordance with Section 54956 of
the Government Code of the State of California.

MALONEY:  Councilmember MALONEY entered Council Chambers at 5:16 p.m.

PUBLIC COMMENT FOR NON-AGENDIZED ITEMS – F2M25-4

1) Lewis McCAMMON, 105 N. Cordova St, distributed a handout to Council which is on file in the
  City Clerk’s office. He thanked Council for their direction at the last meeting to provide Zoom
  access to the Historic Preservation Commission meeting. He went on to discuss an agenda item
  from the City Council meeting on June, 24, 2024 for the Amended Plan for the amended plan for
  use of American Rescue Plan Act of 2021 relief funds, and specifically the removal of funds for
  the purchase of a fire truck. He went on to discuss an article from the New York Times regarding
  the difficulties agencies have faced in obtaining fire trucks. Mr. McCammon went on to discuss
  federal budget cuts to HUD programs and staff and referred to another article from the Affordable
  Housing Source.

CONSENT AGENDA (Item Nos. 1 – 14)

All items listed under the Consent Agenda, with the exception of Item Nos. 7 and 14, were considered
by the City Council to be routine and were enacted by one motion.

  1
2-24-25
 1.  ADOPTION OF A RESOLUTION TERMINATING THE EXISTENCE OF A LOCAL
  EMERGENCY DUE TO WINDSTORM EVENT – F2M25-20, R2M25-9

  Staff requested that the City Council adopt a resolution terminating the existence of a local
  emergency due to the recent windstorm and extreme fire weather. In addition to the Governor
  of California declaring a state of emergency on January 7, 2025, Los Angeles County
  proclaimed the existence of a local emergency that same day due to the windstorm event wind
  that caused extreme conditions such as massive fires, power outages, damage to power poles
  and utilities infrastructure and fallen trees, impacting transportation arteries, requiring repair
  and threatening the integrity of the City’s infrastructure. On January 13, 2025, the Alhambra
  City Council declared the existence of a local emergency and ratified the City Manager’s
  Proclamation of Existence of a Local Emergency on January 7, 2025 due to the windstorm
  event. The conditions pertaining to the windstorm event response no longer warranted and
  necessitated the existence of a local emergency.

  Discussion:  None.

  Action Taken:  City Council adopted Resolution No. R2M25-9 entitled: A Resolution
  of the City Council of the City of Alhambra, California, terminating the existence of a Local
  Emergency

  Vote:  Moved:  MALONEY  Seconded:  ANDRADE-STADLER
  Ayes:  ANDRADE-STADLER, MAZA, LEE, MALONEY, WANG
  Noes:  NONE
  Absent:  NONE

2.  NOTICE INVITING BIDS: 2025 USDA SUMMER FOOD SERVICE PROGRAM – F2M25-25,
  N2M25-18

  The Summer Food Service Program (SFSP) is a federally funded program administered by
  the State of California Department of Education. The proposed SFSP would begin distributing
  lunches and snacks on June 2, 2025 and will provided Monday through Friday through August
  8, 2025. The City would be eligible for reimbursement by the California Department of
  Education for lunches, snacks and operational costs.

  Discussion:  None.

  Action Taken:  City Council approved the City’s participation in the 2025 Summer
  Food Service Program; authorized staff to circulate a Notice Inviting Bids to secure a vendor
  to provide prepared lunches and snacks for the program; and, directed staff to undertake the
  steps necessary to finalize Council’s action.

  Vote:  Moved:  MALONEY  Seconded:  ANDRADE-STADLER
  Ayes:  ANDRADE-STADLER, MAZA, LEE, MALONEY, WANG
  Noes:  NONE
  Absent:  NONE

3.  ACCEPT A DONATION OF A SCOREBOARD FROM EAST ALHAMBRA LITTLE
  LEAGUE AND APPROPRIATION OF FUNDS FOR INSTALLATION – F2M25-12,
M2M25-17

  2
2-24-25
   El Camino Chevrolet donated a scoreboard and remote control to East Alhambra Little League
  (EALL). EALL wanted to donate the scoreboard to the City of Alhambra for use a the Almansor
  Park baseball field. The scoreboard was eight feet wide by six feet high. Installation required
  trenching for the placement of conduits to run new electrical lines and connect to an existing
  power source. Staff received three bids for the installation of the scoreboard. The lowest
  responsible bid was $10,000. EALL donated $10,000 to cover the costs of the scoreboard
  installation. After installation, the City would provide for ongoing maintenance of the
  scoreboard, but EALL would assume the responsibility for the remote-control system.

  Discussion:  None.

  Action Taken:  City Council accepted from East Alhambra Little League a donation of
  an electric outdoor baseball scoreboard at Almansor Park baseball field; accepted a cash
  donation of $10,000 for the installation of the scoreboard; directed the Finance Director to
  appropriate the $10,000 in revenues and expenditures for the completion of the project; and,
  directed staff to undertake the steps necessary to finalize Council’s action. (M2M25-17)

  Vote:  Moved:  MALONEY  Seconded:  ANDRADE-STADLER
  Ayes:  ANDRADE-STADLER, MAZA, LEE, MALONEY, WANG
  Noes:  NONE
  Absent:  NONE

4.  NOTICE OF COMPLETION: FIRE STATION 73 KITCHEN REMODEL PROJECT –
  F2M23-49, C2M24-45, M2M25-18

  On June 24, 2024, the City Council awarded a contract to First Trade LLC dba YMC for the
  Fire Station 73 Kitchen Remodel Project in the amount of $165,000. There was one change
  order issued in the amount of $5,399.81. The change order was issued for unforeseen
  additional services related to the gas line and electrical adjustments. The total cost of the
  project was $170,339.81. The project was completed in accordance with the City’s
  requirements and specifications. As such it would be appropriate for the City Council to accept
  the project as complete and instruct the City Clerk that the Notice of Completion be filed with
  the County of Los Angeles Recorder’s Office.

  Discussion:  None.

  Action Taken:  City Council accepted the work of First Trade LLC dba YMC for the
  Fire Station 73 Kitchen Remodel Project as complete in the amount of $170,399.81; directed
  the City Clerk to file a Notice of Completion with County of Los Angeles for recordation;
  instructed the Finance Director to release the five percent retention 35 days from the date of
  recordation, if no liens are filed; and, directed staff to undertake the steps necessary to finalize
  Council’s action. (M2M25-18)

  Vote:  Moved:  MALONEY  Seconded:  ANDRADE-STADLER
  Ayes:  ANDRADE-STADLER, MAZA, LEE, MALONEY, WANG
  Noes:  NONE
  Absent:  NONE

5.  APPROVE STATE OF CALIFORNIA GOVERNOR’S OFFICE OF EMERGENCY SERVICES
  (CAL OES) DESIGNATION OF APPLICANT’S AGENT RESOLUTION FOR FEDERAL AND
  STATE FINANCIAL ASSISTANCE – F2M20-33, F2M25-20, M2M25-19

  3
2-24-25
   On January 13, 2025, the City Council adopted Resolution No. R2M25-1 proclaiming the
  existence of a local emergency. On January 7, 2025, a destructive widespread windstorm and
  extreme fire weather impacted the Los Angeles metropolitan area, including the County of Los
  Angeles and the City of Alhambra. This weather system caused extreme conditions such as
  power outages, fallen trees and damages to the City’s infrastructure. For Alhambra to request
  the funding assistance, the City Council must designate City agents responsible for providing
  required assurances and executing agreements with FEMA and Cal OES on behalf of the City
  and approve the corresponding Cal OES Form 130. Staff recommended the City Manager,
  Fire Chief and Finance Director be designated, and be effective for all open and future
  disasters declared by the state or federal government up to three years following the date of
  approval by City Council so as to expedite the processing of requests in the future.

  Discussion:  None.

  Action Taken:  City Council approved that certain State of California Governor’s Office
  of Emergency Services Designation of Applicant’s Agent Resolution for Non-State Agencies
  (OES-FPD-130) a copy of which is on file in the City Clerk’s Office as Cal OES ID No. 037-
  00884 and by this reference incorporated herein and made a part of as though fully set forth
  herein; and, directed staff to undertake the steps necessary to finalize Council’s action.
  (M2M25-19).

  Vote:  Moved:  MALONEY  Seconded:  ANDRADE-STADLER
  Ayes:  ANDRADE-STADLER, MAZA, LEE, MALONEY, WANG
  Noes:  NONE
  Absent:  NONE

6.  AWARD CONTRACT: ROOF REPLACEMENT AT THE UTILITIES CUSTOMER
  SERVICE CENTER – F2M24-69, N2M24-152, C2M25-7, M2M25-20

  At the December 9, 2024 meeting, the City Council approved the distribution of a Notice
  Inviting Bids for the Roof Replacement at the Utilities Customer Service Center project. On
  February 13, 2025, the City Clerk received eight bids that ranged from $64,400 to $139,950.
  Staff reviewed the bids received and the bid from McDonnell Roofing, Inc. in the amount of
  $64,400 was the lowest responsible bid. McDonnell Roofing, Inc. had the necessary licenses
  to complete the work and has conducted similar projects.

  Discussion:  None.

  Action Taken:  City Council awarded a contract, subject to final language approval by
  the City Manager and City Attorney, to McDonnell Roofing, Inc. in the amount of $64,400.00
  for the Roof Replacement at the Customer Service Center; and, directed staff to undertake
  the steps necessary to finalize the Council’s action. (M2M25-20)

  Vote:  Moved:  MALONEY  Seconded:  ANDRADE-STADLER
  Ayes:  ANDRADE-STADLER, MAZA, LEE, MALONEY, WANG
  Noes:  NONE
  Absent:  NONE

7.  AMEND RESERVE POLICY – F2M25-17, R2M25-8, M2M25-21

  The reserve policy was updated and approved by the City Council on June 23, 2023,
  designating the following reserve uses: General Fund Emergency Reserve, Legal Liability

  4
2-24-25
   Reserve, Building and Facilities Reserve, and Rolling Stock and Equipment Reserve. The
  General Fund Emergency Reserve was currently funded at 21% of the General Fund operating
  expenditures, totaling $20.5 million, exceeding the 20% goal for FY 2024/25. This reserve was
  designated for natural or fiscal emergencies. Following an evaluation of the City’s risks, guided
  by the Government Finance Officers Association (GFOA) best practices, staff assessed areas
  such as revenue stability, expenditure volatility, risks, leverage, liquidity, capital projects, and
  other factors. Given the moderate to high risks identified, staff recommended increasing the
  General Fund Reserve target to 30% of operating expenditures to enhance financial security
  and better address future uncertainties. Additionally, staff requested the City Council direct
  the Director of Finance to allocate any unappropriated surplus, including future surpluses,
  through appropriation transfers or budget adjustments until the reserve levels are met.
  Separate from the reserve policy, staff worked on addressing the long-term unfunded liabilities.
  A staff report would be brought back to amend the reserve policy in the future to recommend
  creating a new reserve category specifically for unfunded pension liability.

  Public Comment:  Lewis McCAMMON, 105 N. Cordova St., discussed the item and
  questioned the recommendation. He suggested continuing the past practice of presenting all
  changes to reserve funds for Council approval rather than the Director of Finance making
  changes through appropriation transfers or budget adjustments as needed. Mr. McCammon
  suggested making an additional fund called an Undesignated Reserve Fund for unforeseen
  expenses or emergencies.

  Discussion: Mayor WANG and Director of Finance LIEU discussed the existing process for
  handling surplus, the Building and Facilities Reserve, and the proposed policy for distributing
  surplus funds to the reserve funds.

  Vice Mayor LEE and Ms. LIEU discussed staff recommendations for reallocation of funds
  based on staff’s knowledge of Council’s Strategic Plan Goals, Council’s ability to add additional
  reserve categories, and Council’s establishment of the current reserve funds in 2018. Ms. LEE
  supported the increase of the goal to 30%. Ms. LEE and City Manager BINNQUIST discussed
  a potential study session to review the reserve funds, the past staff reports in 2018 and 2023,
  and the second amendment to the policy presented at this evening’s agenda. Ms. BINNQUIST
  further discussed the intention of the amended policy to ensure financial stability, address
  potential emergency expenses, and make up for any delays to reimbursement for emergency
  expenses such as the recent windstorm and wildfires. Ms. LEE requested an additional study
  session to review each reserve category and expressed concern with automatically adding to
  predetermined funds which may not be necessary for each year. Ms. LIEU went on to discuss
  the creation of the reserves in response to unfunded liabilities.

  Ms. WANG surmised that there was a desire for better understanding of the reserves, how
  they were built, and supported Ms. Lee’s suggestion of a workshop with staff and Council to
  study the reserve funds.

  Councilmember MALONEY tried to recall the discussions in 2018 to establish the funds,
  supported the increase to the General Funds Emergency Reserve goal to 30%, the purpose
  of the funds, and supported the suggestion for either a special Council meeting or a study
  session to review the funds. Councilmember ANDRADE-STADLER discussed the uncertainty
  of federal funding due to budget cuts and supported a study session to review the reserve
  funds, and supported the increase to the General Funds Emergency Reserve goal to 30%.

  Councilmember MAZA supported a study session to review the reserve funds. Mr. MAZA and
  Ms. LIEU discussed the average annual surplus of funds which was dependent on factors such
  as staff vacancies. Mr. MAZA and Ms. LIEU also discussed the ability to give staff discretion
  as to allocation of funds to each reserve fund. Mr. MAZA supported this aspect.

  5
2-24-25
   Ms. WANG agreed with Council’s consensus to increase to the General Funds Emergency
  Reserve goal to 30%, and to establish financial stability. Ms. WANG proposed and amendment
  to the resolution that having staff recommendations regarding surplus allocations return to the
  City Council for public review would help ensure alignment with Strategic Plan priorities and to
  have a more transparent process. City Attorney MONTES offered clarification as to the current
  process and the proposed process. Ms. WANG and Ms. ANDRADE-STADLER discussed her
  suggestion as well as the proposed study session to review the reserve funds. Ms. LIEU
  discussed the Finance Department’s Audited Financial Statement and the Mid-Year Budget
  Review. Ms. ANDRADE-STADLER went on to discuss the need for emergency reserve funds
  in the event of unforeseen cataclysmic circumstances. Mr. MAZA and Ms. LIEU continued to
  discuss the ways in which the reserve funds have addressed unfunded liabilities, excluding
  pension costs. Ms. WANG responded to Ms. ANDRADE-STADLER’s comments regarding
  unforeseen emergencies.

  Ms. WANG motioned to approve the increase to the General Funds Emergency Reserve goal
  to 30%, but to not adopt Section 3 of the Resolution related to the administrative allocation
  process for surplus funds. Ms. ANDRADE-STADLER seconded the motion.

  Action Taken:  City Council adopted Resolution No. R2M25-8 entitled: A Resolution
  of the City Council of the City of Alhambra to amend the General Fund Reserve Policy with a
  modification to the language of the Resolution – specifically, the removal of Section 3 of the
  Resolution, amending the General Fund Reserve Policy to increase the General Fund
  Emergency Reserve goal to 30%; and, directed staff to undertake the steps necessary to
  finalize the Council’s action. (M2M25-21)

  Vote:  Moved:  WANG  Seconded:  ANDRADE-STADLER
  Ayes:  MAZA, LEE, MALONEY, ANDRADE-STADLER, WANG
  Noes:  NONE
  Absent:  NONE

8.  NOTICE INVITING BIDS: 2024 CDBG ADA RAMP PROJECT – F2M25-26, N2M25-20

  Staff requested that the City Council approve the distribution of a Notice Inviting Bids for the
  2024 CDBG ADA Ramp Project. The project was located in the southwest, central, and
  northeast areas of the City. The project consisted of the construction of thirty-nine (39) base
  bid curb ramps and ancillary components such as curb & gutter, cross gutter, and sidewalks.
  Plans and specifications were prepared for this project which were reviewed by staff and were
  in conformance with the City’s standards. Once approved, they would be posted and
  advertised with the bid notice and bid instructions.

  Discussion:  None.

  Action Taken:  City Council authorized the distribution of Notice Inviting Bids for the
  2024 CDBG ADA Ramp Project, with bids due no later than 10:30 a.m. on Thursday, March
  27, 2025; and, directed staff to undertake the steps necessary to finalize the Council’s action.

  Vote:  Moved:  MALONEY  Seconded:  ANDRADE-STADLER
  Ayes:  ANDRADE-STADLER, MAZA, LEE, MALONEY, WANG
  Noes:  NONE
  Absent:  NONE

  6
2-24-25
 9.  NOTICE INVITING BIDS: ALLEY REHABILITATION PROJECT (AREA A - PHASE II)
  – F2M25-27, N2M25-21

  The Alley Rehabilitation (Area A / Phase II) Project consisted of 5 alley segments and 1
  alternate location. The alley segments were categorized as failed condition. Staff prepared
  specifications for distribution to qualified firms to submit proposals for the preparation of Plans,
  Specifications, and Estimates (PS&E) documents. The project was located on Curtis Lane
  (Alley) and Olive Place (Alley), between Shorb Street and Valley Boulevard.

  Discussion:  None.

  Action Taken:  City Council authorized the circulation of a Notice Inviting Bids to
  prospective contractors for the Alley Rehabilitation Project (Area A / Phase II) with bids due no
  later than 10:30 a.m. on Thursday, March 20, 2025; and, directed staff to undertake the steps
  necessary to finalize Council’s action.

  Vote:  Moved:  MALONEY  Seconded:  ANDRADE-STADLER
  Ayes:  ANDRADE-STADLER, MAZA, LEE, MALONEY, WANG
  Noes:  NONE
  Absent:  NONE

14.  RESOLUTION: APPOINTMENTS REQUIRED IN CONNECTION  WITH  THE
  REORGANIZATION OF THE CITY COUNCIL – F2M25-24, R2M25-10

  The following action was required to be taken in connection with the reorganization of the City
  Council; i.e., designating the City’s Board members to the Los Angeles County Sanitation
  District Nos. 2 and 16. By the District’s bylaws, Katherine Lee, by virtue of becoming Mayor,
  was the City’s Member; and, Jeff Maloney was an alternate member to act in place of the
  presiding officer of the Alhambra City Council.

  Discussion:  Mayor WANG discussed her position as Mayor on various Boards such
  as the Sanitation District and encouraged her colleagues to provide continuity in
  representation. She offered herself as an alternate should any Councilmember not be able to
  fulfill their duties. Vice Mayor LEE stated that during her time as Vice Mayor, she attended
  each meeting via Zoom and agreed with Ms. Wang’s comments regarding the importance of
  attendance. Councilmember MALONEY agreed with Ms. Wang’s comments regarding the
  importance of continuity and stated that as incoming Vice Mayor he would closely monitor the
  meetings to ensure a smooth transition during his rotation as Vice Mayor and Mayor.

  Action Taken:  City Council adopted Resolution No. R2M25-10 entitled: A Resolution
  of the Alhambra City Council pertaining to the designation of the Member and Alternate
  Member of the Boards of Directors of County Sanitation District Nos. 2 and 16 of Los Angeles
  County

  Vote:  Moved:  ANDRADE-STADLER  Seconded:  MALONEY
  Ayes:  LEE, ANDRADE-STADLER, MALONEY, MAZA, WANG
  Noes:  NONE

2-24-25

with the consent of the City Council, adjourned the special meeting.
